name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets leaned on the biggest AI-linked tech firms, so doubts about AI hit the whole index. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12 and a selloff followed. Official papers warned that AI [[valuation]]s look stretched, and the S&P 500 fell four straight weeks.
today: Nvidia's board approved Huang's return and Reuters says Trump pressured the company to do it. The stock rose 30% or more and the S&P 500 had its best day since April 2025. The cheering came with pushback. Members of both parties in Congress questioned Trump's view that Huang is not a national security risk. Treasury Secretary Bessent reversed his harder line on Nvidia. Staff allegations of workplace abuse surfaced, and one headline mentions a reported SEC probe. A strategist warned that Wall Street is not pricing in a data center slowdown. HPE posted its strongest growth ever but its stock wavered, which shows even good AI news does not lift everything.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up headline inflation. Central banks must decide whether the price jump fades or leaks into wages and services. Euro area inflation hit 4%, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
today: Fed's John Williams said higher interest rates are likely 'over time' to address inflation. He also said he is confident inflation gets closer to 2% in 2027. Waller said the Fed meets Dec 8 and 9. Cook said damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep oil prices high for a long time. Japan's core inflation hit its highest this year as an energy subsidy ended. Friday's note said FTSE futures slipped on a hawkish read of US rates. The 2-year yield is 4.63%, above the Fed's 3.875% rate, so markets already price some hikes.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict began in early 2026 and cut global oil output by 12 mb/d in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned. The IEA says the Hormuz shock lifted the world's oil and gas import bill 25% to $1.6 trillion.
today: WTI fell 4.29% to 80.38, its lowest settle since August. Oil kept flowing out of the Persian Gulf even though tanker attacks continue. Another headline says China has become the top oil buyer. Earlier this week Trump suggested recent gas price drops are tied to the election, calling it 'a giant hoax' in one headline. The Bank of Japan's speech noted that oil is below its April peak but still fairly high.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout. Markets asked how divided government might change tariffs, spending and the dollar. The dollar then had its biggest rally since 2024.
today: The dollar index rose 0.49% to 104.32. Headlines credit hawkish Fed bets, not the election. Goldman Sachs expects the rally to continue in the coming months and fade in 2027. Its technical read says the dollar is overbought and could slow. Sterling and the euro edged up in the morning as the stock rebound took some shine off the dollar. By the close the dollar was higher again.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the currency market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The BOJ's 1.25% rate is 2.625 percentage points below the Fed's 3.875%, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars. Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.
today: USD/JPY was 159.32, down 0.04%, so the yen was little changed. The BOJ chief played down soft consumption data and signaled a near-term rate hike. Japan's inflation accelerated, and the country posted a sixth straight monthly trade deficit. A Reuters-style analysis says BOJ ambiguity on the path of hikes could tempt yen bears. In Friday's Asian session, the Nikkei fell 2.9% on chip and metals stocks.
